title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: The seminal Transformer architecture replacing recurrence and convolutions with multi-head self-attention mechanisms.

insights.question: Can sequence transduction models be built entirely without recurrence or convolution, relying solely on multi-head self-attention?
insights.methodology: Scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention mechanisms, and sinusoidal positional encodings evaluated on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation benchmarks.
insights.findings: Achieved state-of-the-art 28.4 BLEU on En-De (+2.0 BLEU over best ensemble) and 41.8 BLEU on En-Fr, training in only 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs.
insights.contributions: Introduced the Transformer architecture, establishing the foundational paradigm for all modern Large Language Models (LLMs).
insights.limitations: Quadratic memory and compute complexity O(N²) with sequence length; lack of inherent recurrence requires explicit positional encodings.

title: SCHOLAR: A Local-First Research Assistant for Scientific Papers
summary: An offline-capable, local-first research assistant providing inspectable citation grounding with pixel-level PDF bounding box coordinates.

insights.question: How can an AI assistant provide strict-local, zero-cloud verification of scientific claims with inspectable visual bounding boxes on original PDF pages?
insights.methodology: Document AST parsing into multimodal nodes (Text, Tables, Figures, Equations), hybrid BM25 + Dense RRF retrieval, and rule-based Verifier checking numerical match, polarity, and lexical overlap before generation.
insights.findings: Maintains an 87.6% Supported grounding category with 0% ungrounded hallucinations on benchmark evaluations, running hermetically on consumer hardware via local Ollama models.
insights.contributions: First open-source, local-first scientific paper copilot combining Evidence AST extraction, coordinate-preserving visual bounding boxes, and an interactive Evidence Graph API.
insights.limitations: Dependent on local GPU/CPU compute for generation latency; PDF parsing quality depends on OCR/layout fidelity for scanned or degraded manuscripts.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary: Residual learning framework (ResNet) enabling networks of substantially deeper depth (up to 152 layers) to be trained easily.

insights.question: Why do deeper neural networks degrade in training accuracy, and can residual skip connections overcome the degradation problem?
insights.methodology: Identity shortcut connections added to stacked convolutional layers (F(x) + x), allowing optimization of residual mappings rather than unreferenced mappings; tested up to 152 layers on ImageNet.
insights.findings: ResNet-152 achieves 3.57% top-5 error on ImageNet test set, winning 1st place in ILSVRC 2015 while being deeper yet having lower complexity than VGG nets.
insights.contributions: Introduced residual learning formulation that solved the degradation problem and enabled training of 100+ layer networks.
insights.limitations: Requires careful batch normalization tuning; early residual blocks can have representation bottlenecks before deep features emerge.
